thread:
maddie: Heads-up — we need a quick sync on the continuous-batching metrics for the console and routing policy teams. Goal: final list of runtime/infra signals we can reliably surface and alert on.

kevin: +1. Product cares about batch-size distribution heatmaps and p95 wait time by route. UX wants a compact summary card for the console. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

dmitri: For runtime I'm thinking these primitives: batch_count_total, batches_by_size_bucket, tokens_per_batch_histogram, batch_wait_time_seconds (histogram), queue_depth_gauge per worker, worker_saturation_ratio. Keep labels low-cardinality (model, route, region, tier).

carla: Low-cardinality is the big constraint. We can't attach prompt_length/input_hash/etc. Also we should avoid per-request labels (user_id, session).

maddie: Agreed. Can we pick explicit buckets for batch size? product wants fine-grain at small sizes (1-8) and coarser after.

sanjay: Proposed buckets: 1,2,3,4,5-8,9-16,17-32,33-64,65+. Works with Prom histogram.

dmitri: That distribution looks good. Also decide whether to expose wait time as histogram vs summary. Prom histograms + exemplars would let us attach trace ids for slow samples.

carla: Note: our batches are often <200ms lifecycle. If scrape interval is 15s we'll miss per-batch spikes. Need push or internal aggregator that emits rollups (per-second or per-10s).

telemetry-bot: Suggested metric names (draft):
```
redwood_batches_total{model,route,region,tier}
redwood_batch_size_bucket{model,route,region,tier,le}
redwood_batch_wait_seconds_bucket{model,route,region,tier,le}
redwood_batch_tokens_sum{model,route,region,tier}
redwood_batch_queue_depth{model,route,region,tier}
redwood_worker_saturation{worker_id? (internal only)}
```

maddie: For worker_id let's keep it internal to infra metrics (no console label). Console will show aggregated per-pool.

kevin: Console wants these views: 1) real-time mini-heatmap (batch size distribution over last 5m), 2) per-route p50/p95/p99 wait time sparkline, 3) saturation indicator with colour states (ok, high, critical).

dmitri: Alerting proposals: p95 wait_time > 200ms for 1m on production routes -> ticket; queue_depth > 100 for 30s -> paging; worker_saturation > 0.85 for 2m -> auto-scale hook. Need agreement on thresholds per tier.

carla: Implementation notes: runtime will emit per-batch samples to a local aggregator that maintains time-windowed histograms (10s windows). Aggregator publishes rollups to collector every 10s. We'll also emit counters for total_batches and total_tokens for long-term aggregates.

sanjay: Telemetry path: runtime -> sidecar aggregator -> telemetry-ingest (Kafka) -> OTLP collector -> Prom-compatible TSDB. This preserves short-lived signals. Do we have capacity in ingest for 10s granularity?

dmitri: We do but need to cap cardinality. Plan: only (model,route,region,tier) labels and a boolean kv_cache_hit label if that helps. That doubles series but manageable.

maddie: UX + Alerts owner: kevin. Runtime + infra owners: dmitri + carla. Telemetry infra: sanjay. Let's schedule 30m hangout to finalise buckets and thresholds. Proposed: tomorrow 10am PT.

kevin: Works for me. I'll mock the console card (static mock) before meeting so we can align on data shape.

carla: Will push a prototype aggregator payload schema to the design doc and drop a sample payload in the meeting thread.

telemetry-bot: Note: please include the following in the design doc: cardinality estimate, expected series count per 1k RPS, example query for heatmap, and alert runbook links.

maddie: Thanks — quick next steps: kevin mock, carla schema, dmitri runtime instrumentation PR, sanjay ingest capacity check. Meeting invite sent. :thumbsup:
